items.title: Library supplement: Canonical total radial extension

source.attribution: Generic exposition of classical sphere calculus; no primary-textbook completion or novelty claim.

items.statement: Write \(E_n=\mathbb R^{n+1}\), \(S_n=\{x\in E_n:\|x\|=1\}\), and \(M_{n,N}=S_n^{\operatorname{Fin}N}\). The dimensions are natural numbers and may be zero. For every natural \(n\), every type \(A\) equipped only with a specified element \(0_A\), every function \(h:S_n\to A\), and every \(z\in E_n\), define the value by radial normalization when \(z\ne0\) and by \(0_A\) when \(z=0\). No topology, norm, measurability, or regularity of \(A\) or \(h\) is required by this definition. The original source D3 uses \(A=\mathbb R\) or \(A=E_n\); this is a pure literal-definition generalization, identical on both of those original codomains.
assumptions: Use the indicated canonical real Euclidean, unit-sphere and finite-product carriers; no positive-dimension restriction is imposed.
This is a definition or abbreviation. It imposes no unstated regularity, tangency, integrability or probability hypothesis.
The codomain is any type with a distinguished zero. No topology or algebra beyond that point is required.
